title: Choose the V2 structure
question: The K-SMART visual world is settled and pinned, so this choice is composition only: how the dashboard organises itself. The roll dealt three structures. Lock one, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Scope Bar + Canvas
options.lineage: the scope line officials already speak: Kollam, building permission, delayed
options.thesis: The five cascading dropdowns collapse into one scope line, and everything below the line is the answer to it.
options.viewport: A single scope bar carries the current question as removable tokens (Kerala · All modules · Upto today). The navy hero and the context strip are both gone; the four file-status figures sit immediately under the bar at full scale, with the SLI breach chart below them. Adding a filter adds a token; removing one removes a token.
options.risk: Officials used to five labelled dropdowns may not realise the bar is where filtering now lives.

options.label: Module Board
options.lineage: the departmental wall board a secretary scans each morning
options.thesis: Every module gets an equal tile, so the whole local body's health reads in one screen before anyone filters anything.
options.viewport: A compact context row, then a grid of module tiles — Civil Registration, Building Permission, Property Tax, Finance, Meeting Management, Grievance, Business Facilitation — each showing its delayed count, its disposal rate and a short trend. Selecting a tile expands it in place into the full KPI and chart set, rather than navigating away.
options.risk: Equal weighting treats a healthy module and a burning one the same until you read the numbers.

options.label: Status Ledger
options.lineage: the file register every local body office already keeps
options.thesis: One ledger where every local body is a row and its file status is a proportional bar, so comparison needs no chart at all.
options.viewport: The four state figures sit in the ledger's own header as the Kerala-wide total, then every local body follows as a row carrying a single proportional bar split into disposed, under process and delayed. Rows sort by breach rate by default, so the worst performer is the first thing read. Sorting is the navigation; there is no separate chart.
options.risk: A dense ledger is powerful on a desk monitor and demands real work to hold up on a phone.
